title: Mashup madness
content_html:
What You'll Do

In this project you're the AI director, chaining several AI tools together into one finished piece — a technique called a mashup pipeline. Instead of using one tool on its own, you'll pass work from tool to tool: a chatbot writes an idea, an image generator turns it into a picture, a text-to-speech tool gives it a voice, and a design tool stitches it all into a poster, comic or mini-campaign.

You'll discover that different AI tools have different specialities (text, image, sound, layout) — just like a film crew has a writer, an artist, a voice actor and an editor. You'll also see how what comes out of one tool depends on how good the prompt from the previous step was.

By the end you'll have one complete "AI Mashup" — say a campaign poster for a made-up product, a story page with illustration and narration, or a brand for an invented character — built entirely by chaining tools.

What You'll Need

  • A chatbot (text): ChatGPT (chat.openai.com) or Microsoft Copilot (copilot.microsoft.com).
  • An image generator: Bing Image Creator (bing.com/images/create), or Craiyon (craiyon.com, no login) as a backup.
  • A text-to-speech tool: TTSMaker (ttsmaker.com, free, no login).
  • A tool to put it together: Canva (canva.com) or Google Slides.
  • Good to know: you're using 3–4 tools, each with its own free limits — write a good prompt the first time rather than burning credits on rushed tries.

Steps

  1. See the pipeline. The flow is: Idea → Text AI → Image AI → Audio AI → Assembled final product.
  2. Pick a brief. Choose one: "a mascot and poster for a Nairobi recycling campaign," "a new snack brand," or "a page from a picture book about a magical animal." Write it at the top of your doc.
  3. Get the core idea from the chatbot. Try: "I'm designing a mascot and short slogan for a [recycling campaign / snack brand / picture book]. Give me: 1) a character name and short personality, 2) a one-sentence slogan, 3) a vivid visual description I can use to generate an image." Then refine with a follow-up like "make the character friendlier, add bright colours."
  4. Turn the description into an image. Paste the visual description into your image generator and add style words: "A friendly cartoon robot made of recycled bottles, big round eyes, holding a recycling bin, flat illustration style, bright colours, white background."
  5. Generate and choose. Make 2–3 versions, compare, and pick the best — or fix the prompt ("remove the extra arm," "plain white background").
  6. Add a voice line. Ask the chatbot: "Write a short, catchy 10-second line this character would say to encourage recycling." Paste it into TTSMaker, pick a voice, and download the clip.
  7. Assemble it. In Canva or Slides, build one poster/slide with the character image, the slogan, the voice line (and its audio if you can embed it), and the brief title. Keep the layout neat — image one side, text the other.
  8. Present. Show your mashup in under a minute, saying which tool did what and one thing you had to fix or re-prompt.

Examples to Try

  • "Bao the Bottle Robot": a recycling mascot — chatbot made the name, personality and slogan ("Bao says: don't waste it, recycle it!"), image tool drew a robot made of bottles, TTSMaker voiced a cheerful jingle, all combined into a one-page Canva poster.
  • "Mango Blast" snack brand: chatbot wrote the tagline ("sunshine in every bite!") and packaging idea, image tool made the packet design, final slide shows a mock advert with a voiced script.
  • Picture-book page "Nia and the Cloud Whale": chatbot wrote two story sentences and a whale description, image tool drew it, TTSMaker narrated it, final slide looks like a storybook page you can play aloud.

Tips

  • Broken output? (Distorted faces, extra limbs, garbled text.) That's a real AI limit — ask "what went wrong here?" instead of hiding it.
  • Watch for prompt drift. If you describe your character one way to the chatbot and differently to the image tool, the result won't match — information gets lost as it passes between tools, just like in a real production line. Reuse the same key words.
  • Blocked request? Image and text tools refuse some things (violence, real people). That's expected — reword it.
  • Keep Craiyon handy if Bing is slow or you can't sign in.

Think About It

  • What is an "AI pipeline," and why can chaining tools make something a single tool couldn't?
  • Which tool struggled most to follow your instructions? Why?
  • How much of your final mashup was "made by you" versus "made by the AI"?
  • Give one example of how changing a prompt changed what the next tool produced.
  • What real jobs or products (adverts, games, apps, music videos) probably combine multiple AI tools like you did?

Challenge Yourself

  • Easy: Add a second character who interacts with the first — a new image and a line of dialogue.
  • Medium: Turn your mashup into a 3-panel comic: three story beats from the chatbot, a consistent-style image per panel (reuse the character description), plus speech bubbles.
  • Hard: Build a full mini-campaign — slogan + script, poster, voiced advert, and a simple animation (Canva's animate feature) — and pitch it in 60 seconds, naming each tool's role and one ethical question (could the mascot mislead people? whose style was the AI trained on?).
